definitions.explanation: The time just before death; one's last moments of life.

examples.japanese: {臨終|りんじゅう}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{立|た}ち{会|あ}う→立ち会う：21638_tachiau⟧。
⟦{祖父|そふ}→祖父：01452_sofu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{臨終|りんじゅう}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{間|ま}に{合|あ}わなかった→間に合う：01142_maniau⟧。
examples.english: I didn't make it in time for my grandfather's final moments.

examples.japanese: {臨終|りんじゅう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{際|さい}→際：02819_sai⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{家族|かぞく}→家族：00552_kazoku⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{囲|かこ}まれていた→囲む：02037_kakomu⟧。
examples.english: He was surrounded by family at the time of his passing.

examples.japanese: ⟦{医師|いし}→医師：11851_ishi⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{臨終|りんじゅう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{告|つ}げる→告げる：11808_tsugeru⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧、⟦{病室|びょうしつ}→病室：21074_byoushitsu⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{静|しず}まり{返|かえ}った→静まり返る：14630_shizumarikaeru⟧。
examples.english: When the doctor announced the passing, the hospital room fell completely silent.

notes:
{臨|りん} (to face, to be present at) + {終|じゅう} (end). A solemn word describing the moment of approaching death. Originally a Buddhist term referring to the final moments before entering the next life.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {臨終|りんじゅう}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{立|た}ち{会|あ}う→立ち会う：21638_tachiau⟧: be present at someone's deathbed
- {臨終|りんじゅう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{迎|むか}える→迎える：01193_mukaeru⟧: face one's final moments
- {臨終|りんじゅう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{告|つ}げる→告げる：11808_tsugeru⟧: announce someone's passing
- {臨終|りんじゅう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{言葉|ことば}→言葉：02880_kotoba⟧: last words
- {臨終|りんじゅう}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{間|ま}に{合|あ}う→間に合う：01142_maniau⟧: make it in time for someone's final moments

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{最期|さいご}→最期：30329_saigo⟧: one's final moments, death — more literary and emotional
- {死|し}に{際|ぎわ}: the verge of death — emphasizes the boundary between life and death
- ⟦{往生|おうじょう}→往生：12704_oujou⟧: passing away (Buddhist) — implies a peaceful death and rebirth in paradise

USAGE:
A formal and respectful word. Commonly heard in hospital settings when a doctor informs family members of a patient's passing. The phrase {臨終|りんじゅう}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{立|た}ち{会|あ}う→立ち会う：21638_tachiau⟧ (to be present at someone's deathbed) is considered important in Japanese culture.
